title: HELP Appeal appoints clinical and infrastructure consultant
summary: Julie Holroyd has been appointed to the role.
body_markdown:
HELP Appeal Photo


The HELP Appeal, the only charity in the United Kingdom dedicated to funding NHS hospital helipads, has appointed Julie Holroyd as clinical and infrastructure consultant.


This is a new role, which will aim to help NHS trusts build safe, effective helipad provision into hospital development plans and improve patients’ access to emergency and specialist care.


Holroyd brings experience as a hospital operations director for NHS England’s New Hospital Programme and as a cardiology consultant nurse, combining an understanding of clinical care with operational and infrastructure planning.


The appointment comes as the New Hospital Programme and wider NHS estate developments create opportunities to consider helipads early in hospital design.


Holroyd will engage trusts at the planning and business case stages, helping them assess where new or improved facilities could support patient care and strengthen services’ resilience.


Working alongside Simon Jones, the HELP Appeal’s technical aviation expert, Holroyd will bring clinical and operational insight to discussions about helipad location, design and use.


Together, they will help NHS trusts consider helipad site safety alongside a patient’s onward journey from landing in a helicopter to treatment, ensuring these needs inform wider hospital plans.


Building on stakeholder discussions already under way, Holroyd explains what’s involved in the new role,


“I look forward to connecting hospital leaders, clinicians, estates teams, aviation specialists and air ambulance services, and supporting a coordinated approach to current and future provision. A key part of my remit will also be identifying projects where the HELP Appeal’s funding could support delivery.”


Robert Bertram, chief executive of the HELP Appeal, added:


“The New Hospital Programme offers a vital opportunity to consider helipad provision from the outset. By bringing Julie’s clinical and operational experience together with Simon’s technical expertise, we can help trusts to plan helipad facilities that meet patients’ needs and operate safely.


“We would like hospitals to speak to us early, while plans are taking shape, so we can help fund helipads that can make a lasting difference to access to emergency care.’


The HELP Appeal funds the construction and upgrading of NHS hospital helipads, helping air ambulances bring seriously ill and injured patients closer to the care they need. Its work is solely supported by charitable donations. Since its creation in 2009, the charity has funded 55 hospital helipads to date, which have seen over 37,000 landings.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the HELP Appeal.*
